summary: Pema Wangchok Gyelpo studied under Shenphen Nangwa, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Khakyab Dorje, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Shenphen Nangwa and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

Pema Wangdi is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned his PhD at James Cook University. His career includes posts at the UN Permanent Mission of Bhutan, the Dzongkha Development Commission, and an adjunct fellowship at Central Queensland University.
Peng Zhou specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a Bachelor of Philosophy from Hunan Normal University in 2017 and a Master of Philosophy from Shaanxi Normal University in 2020.

Penghao Sun works in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied under doctoral supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp, as well as scholars including Qingying Chen, Mark Elliott, Charles Hallisey, Weirong Shen, and Peter K. Bol.
Penor 02 studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang, Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught both Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.

Penor Rinpoche (1933–2009) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Palyul Monastery and founded the Ngagyur Nyingma Institute in 1978. He studied under Thubten Chökyi Dawa, Karma Tekchok Nyingpo, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Pent Nurmekund (1906–1996) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Tartu under Friedrich Ernst Kieckers, Copenhagen under Louis Trolle Hjelmslev, and Paris. He held a teaching and research post at Tartu from 1955 to 1986.

Pentti Aalto (1917–1998) worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at the University of Helsinki and Uppsala under scholars including Gustaf John Ramstedt and Helmer Smith, he served as a docent at Helsinki (1949–1980).

Per Kjeld Sørensen (born 1950) is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Erik Haarh at the University of Copenhagen. He lectured at Copenhagen, served as a professor at the University of Leipzig (1994–2017), and held fellowships at Bonn.

Per Kværne (born 1945) is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his degrees at the University of Oslo under Nils Simonsson. He lectured at the University of Bergen and served as Secretary General of the IATS.

Per Persson (1857–1929) was a linguist who studied at Uppsala University beginning in 1875. He became Professor of Latin Language and Literature at Uppsala University in 1895 and taught students including Jarl Charpentier and Henrik Samuel Nyberg.

Per Vilhelm Hilding Juliusson (1916–1977) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. He completed an M.Theol. at Uppsala University and earned an M.A. and a Ph.D. at Stockholm University, studying under Åke Hultkrantz.

Percy Brown (1872–1955) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the Royal College of Art. He served as Principal of the National College of Arts and Government College of Art and Craft, and curated at the Indian Museum.

Peri Bhaskararao (1947–2021) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor of Phonetics and Phonology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute from circa 1976 to 1998, and later held a post at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Peri Sarveswara Sharma (1926–2000) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He earned his doctorate under Wilhelm Rau between 1967 and 1970 and subsequently held a post at the University of Marburg from circa 1970 to 1991.

Pero Slijepčević (1888–1964) was an Indology scholar who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Fribourg and studied at the University of Geneva. He later served as Professor of Germanistics at the universities of Belgrade and Sarajevo.

Perry Link (born 1944) is a sinologist who completed his B.A. at Harvard University. He taught Chinese language and literature at UCLA, served as an East Asian Studies professor at Princeton, and held a Chancellorial Chair at UC Riverside.

Perry Schmidt-Leukel (born 1954) specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his degrees and habilitation at the University of Munich, and held professorships at the University of Glasgow (2000–2009) and the University of Münster (2009–2023).
Pertti Valtonen (1933–1999) was an Indologist who earned an M.A. from the University of Helsinki by 1964. He also studied under Pentti Aalto until 1968.
Petar Budmani (1835–1914) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Vienna in 1853. He served as a professor at the Dubrovnik Gymnasium from 1868 to 1882.
